m2c/tests/runner/runner_rig.py -- Patch C24: the shared rig of the device tool runner tests.

Why a plain module and not a conftest.py: tests/test_doctor.py does ``from conftest import ...`` (see
tests/headless/headless_rig.py for the same reason).  Each test file imports what it needs from here.

WHAT IS REAL AND WHAT IS FAKE
-----------------------------
Real: the C05 tools (``run_tool`` on a temporary project directory), the C06 policy engine (real rule layers), the
C07 shell tool (real ``bash`` processes), the C08 checkpoints (real blobs under the hermetic ``$M2C_HOME``) and the C02
store (a real SQLite file).  Fake: the link (``FakeLink``: records what the runner sends and checks every payload
against the client's own copy of the protocol schemas, through the link's own strict validator), the person (``ask``
callables the test writes) and, for the ordering tests only, the executor (an injected ``run_tool`` stand-in).

Nothing here looks like a secret: markers are plain words, fake tokens are not needed.

m2c/tests/runner/test_runner_audit_logging.py -- Patch C24: what is recorded locally, and what is never logged.

Build plan 11.4: a log line holds a tool NAME, a call id, a decision and an error code, and nothing else: no input, no
output, no path, no command.  The local audit record (events type ``approval`` + the ``approvals`` table row) holds the
tool, the decision, the scope, who decided and when; its ``input_summary`` column is empty by design.

Real C08 checkpoints, real C05 file tools.  Product guide 8.x / build plan C08: a call that changes files is
checkpointed first; if the checkpoint cannot be saved the call is refused (fail closed); a path that does not exist
yet is fine; ``bash`` cannot be checkpointed and is not.

m2c/tests/runner/test_runner_headless.py -- Patch C24: the adapter for C10's ``install_tool_hooks``.

C10 (headless mode) takes two injected callables, ``decide(proposal)`` and ``execute(proposal)``, and runs a tool only
on an explicit ``allow``.  ``ToolRunner.decide`` / ``ToolRunner.execute`` are shaped for it.  These tests use C10's
OWN hook types and its real ``run_headless`` against the fake device server of the headless tests, so "the hook types
accept them" is proved by the code that consumes them, and so is "a would-ask fails closed there".

m2c/tests/runner/test_runner_interact_headless.py -- Patch L01a: ``m2c -p`` and the two interactive tools.

Headless mode has nobody to ask.  With the runner installed as C10's tool hooks, ``ask_user`` must come back as the
fixed "no person is available to answer" result (``ok`` false) and the run must go on to finish: it never hangs.
``tasks`` still works (there may be no screen, but the list is validated, recorded locally and confirmed).

Until the runner is wired into ``m2c -p`` for real (not part of this patch), a headless run with NO hooks installed
denies every tool call, these two included, exactly as before; that is pinned too.
